summary: Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under numerous teachers, including Rasvir Das and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1959–1967).
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was active in Tibetology and other fields. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and was attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and was taught in 2013 by Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosophy scholar educated at the First Higher School, University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), and University of Freiburg (1920). He served as a professor at Tokyo (1923–1945), dean at Hokkaido University, and professor at Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (born 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. She held positions at the University of Leeds (~1980–2011) and Lancaster University (~2012).

Kim Plofker (born 1964) works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD under David Pingree at Brown University in 1995. Her positions include posts at MIT (2000–2004) and Union College, where she became an associate professor in 2019.

Kimberley C. Patton (born 1958) works in religious studies. She completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1986–1992) and taught there, serving as assistant professor (~1994–2001) and professor of the comparative and historical study of religion (~2001).

Kimiaki Tanaka (born 1955) works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held posts at Tokyo, Beijing Center for Japanese Studies, Keio University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kimmo Koskenniemi (born 1945) works in computational linguistics. He studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and BAULT research community director (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig, supervised by Eli Franco in 2009.
King Pong Chiu works in Indology and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva (1931–2021) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of London (~1959–1962) and served as a professor at the University of Ceylon (~1969–1995).

Kirby Flower Smith (1862–1918) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University (PhD 1889). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and director of the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).
Kirill Solonin (born 1969) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Fo Guang University (~2005–2013) and at Renmin University of China (~2013).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indology scholar who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under several teachers, including Gopinath Bhattacharya and Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1969–1974).
